subject: Hotwash: GPU runway, batching & cache impact ahead of EOY leadership review
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hotwash: GPU runway, batching & cache impact ahead of EOY leadership review

Team —

Quick note to align before the leadership readout next week. I want a short, fact-forward packet that answers three concrete questions for the execs:

1) How many effective GPU-weeks of runway do we have at our current committed + spot mix (by model family)?
2) What unit-cost delta do we get from our current batching + prefix-caching settings vs. an aggressive batching profile?
3) Where are the single biggest operational risk gaps (regions / model variants / customer tiers) that would materially increase spend or latency?

Please keep slides and numbers tight — aim for 1 slide per question and an appendix with the data. I attached the working forecast and the experimental batch/cache heatmap (stubs below).

Immediate asks:
- Vivek: update the GPU runway csv with the 2-week spot burn scenario and a worst-case burst estimate. Highlight assumptions.
- Rishi: call out any SLA / canary mitigations we should promise the customer-facing teams (including failover model variants).
- Lauren: consolidate the final 3 slides and own the one-line exec summary.

Deadline: first draft to me EOD Wednesday 5/15. I'll consolidate and circulate to CEO/CRO on Thursday morning.

Attachments: [gpu-runway-forecast-20280514.csv] (CSV, forecast by pool), [batch-cache-impact-heatmap.pdf] (visual), [cost-sensitivity-scenarios.xlsx]

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hotwash: GPU runway, batching & cache impact ahead of EOY leadership review

Marissa —

Thanks, sending a quick data pass. High-level bullets first:
- Current on-book committed + reserved: ~1,870 GPU-weeks (NVIDIA A100 equiv) for the next quarter. Assumes baseline utilization of 62% across production pools.
- Two-week spot-burn scenario (worst-case): effective runway drops to ~1,520 GPU-weeks; median case is ~1,680 GPU-weeks. I added these as separate columns in the CSV.
- Batching/caching: our conservative profile (max batch 20, prefix-cache TTL 6h) yields ~18% lower token cost vs. the minimal-batch baseline. Aggressive batching (max batch 48, prefetch + longer TTL) adds another ~8–10% savings at the expense of tail P90 latency increases ~15–20% for short prompt workloads. See heatmap for model-family-specific tradeoffs.

Notes / assumptions are embedded in the first tab of gpu-runway-forecast-20280514.csv. Two quick asks for the packet:
1) Please flag any top-3 customers (by spend) that cannot tolerate the latency uplift — we should call those out as exceptions.
2) Sergio, can you add the cross-region failover latency numbers to the appendix? The current sheet has only intra-region numbers.

Attachments (working): [gpu-runway-forecast-20280514.csv], [batch-cache-impact-heatmap.pdf], [cost-sensitivity-scenarios.xlsx]

Vivek
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hotwash: GPU runway, batching & cache impact ahead of EOY leadership review

Thanks — good start. A couple of leadership-level notes:

- Endorse the conservative runway figures; call out the worst-case (two-week spot loss) as the scenario we prepare response runbooks for.
- For the exec slides, please include a one-liner on customer impact for each mitigation (e.g., "Enable aggressive batching for non-interactive embeddings workloads — saves 9% cost, no user-facing latency impact").

Operational asks from my side:
- Add a short canary plan for a staged quantization/quantized-variant rollout: which models safe for 8-bit quant, rollback triggers, and observed quality delta in our evals (put in appendix).
- If we expect a >12% unit-cost delta between current and aggressive batching, we should include a recommendation (opt-in for autoconfig per customer segment).

I'll be available to review the draft after 10am PT Wednesday.

Rishi
VP, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hotwash: GPU runway, batching & cache impact ahead of EOY leadership review

All —

Thanks for the fast turn. I've consolidated the three slides and included the one-line exec summary at the top. Action items (owners + status):

- Vivek: updated runway CSV and scenario columns (DONE) — pulled into appendix tab A.
- Sergio: added cross-region failover numbers and P90 impact (IN PROGRESS).
- Rishi: added canary/rollback triggers and quantization guidance (DONE, see appendix B).
- Marissa: will finalize and circulate to CEO/CRO by Thu 07:30 PT (OWNED).

Notes for the exec summary:
- Net takeaway: runway is sufficient for current demand assuming median spot behavior; we recommend activating a 10% cost-savings plan (targeted aggressive batching + prefix-cache tuning) for background workloads and an opt-in model for latency-sensitive customers.
- Risk: in a two-week spot loss scenario, runway shortfall ~18%, mitigation must be combination of temporary burst purchases + customer-targeted batching opt-ins.

I attached the consolidated 3-slide PDF (working) and flagged the two customer exceptions Vivek noted (AcmeCorp, BetaRetail). Marissa — will wait for your final touches.

Lauren
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Forwarded-attachment stubs referenced: [consolidated-hotwash-3slides.pdf], [gpu-runway-forecast-20280514.csv], [batch-cache-impact-heatmap.pdf]
